prose_updates.tldr: Complete paired interventions yield a synthetic product law and ratio residuals. For the full bounded finite-type class, the proved inverse-modulus result is the bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the sharper upper exponent remains the arbitrary-map incompressible-rigidity question. The radial subclass is sharp at \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse case, this means a full-class \(3/4\) lower exponent versus a \(1/3\) upper exponent, with a sharp radial exponent \(3/4\). Zero-law componentwise circular recovery follows from the direct torus identification argument, not from a converse characterization of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\). The certified Fourier estimator and quotient confidence-set diameter inherit the conservative exponent, giving the primary rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) proves the present zero-law torus conclusion directly and uses those papers only to compare assumptions and conclusion types. Neither comparator supplies a nonzero-error modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf quantify near-isometric representation learning through a different primitive defect. Khesin et al. motivate the volume-preserving kernel, while Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and localized volume-correction context. Milnor supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Compact-manifold density and confidence-set results support the sampling rung, but the propagation exponent here comes from the proved scalar finite-type rigidity lemma.
prose_updates.interpretation: The two exponents answer different certified questions. The localized Hamiltonian family proves that no uniform full-class inverse modulus can improve on the lower obstruction \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). Scalar finite-type rigidity guarantees recovery for every admissible decoder at the more conservative order \(\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\). Radial incompressibility closes this gap, but no corresponding arbitrary-map coercivity theorem has yet been proved. Thus \(3/4\) is sharp for the primary radial model and a lower obstruction for the primary full class, whereas \(1/3\) is the current full-class upper exponent.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The full-class upper exponent is presently \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), obtained from scalar ratio residuals after the complete-law reduction. The desired exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) is proved only for the radial volume-preserving subclass. Symmetrizing the aligned loss does not supply the missing weighted incompressible coercivity, and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}=0\) is not used as a converse test for quotient equivalence. Any counterexample to the sharper upper bound must still arise from legal complete causal law families and respect density, smoothness, conditioning, critical-separation, and attained-order bounds.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general contribution is a full-class bracket: lower exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) and upper exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\). The radial restricted supremum has the sharp exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\). For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the full bracket is \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\), the radial rate is exactly of order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\), and the certified estimator and confidence diameter have rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\). The primary class uses separated critical points and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\geq a_0\), without invoking a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. Plateaus, coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, unknown-order adaptation, and the matching arbitrary-map upper bound remain outside the proved claim.
